provenance.origin: Original project artwork generated with OpenAI ImageGen and assembled in Aseprite 1.3.18.6.

trail.prompt: Redraw the FIRST reference ground fire trail into a clean six-frame 2D pixel-art tile strip for Phi Long Tại Thiên. SECOND reference supplies only the fire color and curves of the two-dragon wave, do NOT draw a dragon. Original trail is too sparse, thin and grainy at native size. Replace it with a single dense continuous flame ribbon anchored to the floor, with a smooth, connected deep crimson foundation and a tangerine-orange center line. Early frames must have a SOLID connected flame base spanning most of the visible width with no dither/no holes, edge taper only at the last tenth of each end. Use two or three broad flame tongues approximately 8 native pixels tall with smooth clean chunky color regions, ember-red dark undersides, orange crest and selective amber hot ridge. Five well-separated colors, neither scattered one-pixel speckles nor noise, no smoke, glow or blur. Draw from elevated top-down 3/4 view, small tongues rising a little from the ground line. Native intended width 50–54 px and full height 12–15 px, same baseline throughout. It must visibly form ONE line when tiled every 24 native pixels. Exact atlas source geometry: 1536×1024, THREE equal columns and TWO equal rows (each 512px square), exactly SIX complete isolated effects, consistent horizontal center and baseline, on PURE BLACK #000000. Within each cell first cel width about 400 px, height about 96 px, center x=256, ground baseline y=282. Chronological sequence: 1 vivid solid orange ridge, 2 gently licking orange, 3 flattening red-orange still continuous, 4 cooling dark red and amber ridge still continuous, 5 one broad fading ember patch with two narrow interruptions, 6 two or three tiny dark ember clusters. Early to middle four frames should be SOLID, then shrink and darken only near the end. No label, guides, ground, characters, weapons, rings, or additional effects. This art is shown around 1x to 2x zoom, prioritize legibility over thin detail.
